summary: the flake ledger matches EXACTLY, the deliberate opposite of the stage 2 guard's prefix match
why: npm test is a strict PREFIX of npm test -- --grep auth, so prefix matching would let a failure recorded for the whole suite mark a narrower run flaky - a false positive on a different suite
risk: two mechanisms in one kit that match command strings differently reads as an inconsistency bug to anyone who finds it; the reason is written at the top of flake-ledger.sh so it survives without me
controls: test-flake-ledger.sh asserts the prefix case is NOT seen

summary: COMMAND NARROWING defeats the flake ledger, and this is stage 3's headline limitation
hole: exact matching also means an agent that hits a red npm test can run npm test -- --grep auth instead; the ledger has no entry for the narrower string, the pass stamps clean, and the gate sees nothing
not_fixed: deliberately - the alternatives were prefix matching, which false-positives across suites, and normalising the command, which guesses. Narrowing is at least a visible act in the transcript
obligation: must be a HEADLINE limitation in the trial record and README, not a footnote

summary: the flake ledger's own fail-open warns on a channel that reaches nobody - a second INC-0013 site
detail: post-bash.sh:66 echoes 'flake detection is NOT enforcing' to stderr, then the hook exits 0 as a PostToolUse. INC-0013 established that a non-blocking hook's output lands in the debug log, so the warning announcing that verification has stopped enforcing is invisible
consequence: if flake-ledger.sh is ever unreadable, every re-run pass stamps clean and looks identical to a first pass
status: OPEN - the warning is correct and loud in the code and useless in practice; closing it needs INC-0013's channel problem solved, not a change here

summary: a declared flake left NO trace a reviewer could ever see - the gate made it deliberate, not visible
found_when: building step 4; the gate accepted a declared flake and allowed the commit, and I went looking for where a second person would learn of it
detail: .claude/.flaky is gitignored and the stamp expires after thirty minutes. A flake could be declared, committed and forgotten with nothing in the repository recording it. 'someone else can see it' is this kit's own criterion for whether a mechanism buys anything, and step 4 did not meet it
fix: f604d45 - verify-gate now refuses a declared-flaky commit carrying no Flaky: trailer, and prints the exact --trailer form
why_the_gate: it is the ONLY place that can require the trailer, because by the time CI runs the stamp is gone

summary: stage 3's CI half is structurally WEAKER than stage 2's and the README must not imply parity
asymmetry: check-test-changes reads the branch DIFF, so an UNDECLARED test change is visible in it. Nothing in the repository records that a commit was made under a flaky stamp, because the stamp is gitignored and gone by CI time
consequence: CI cannot detect a MISSING Flaky: trailer. It can only validate the trailers it finds and make them visible in the PR
one_hole_it_does_close: a Flaky: line typed into the message body records as ZERO trailers - git parses trailers only from the final paragraph - so a checker reading parsed trailers alone would call that commit clean while git log shows the line plainly

summary: stage 2's guard caught its author: I declared 2 controls changing expectation, the suite proved 4
detail: the Test-change declaration for f604d45 initially named two existing controls whose expectation the trailer requirement flips. Running the suite showed four - all four asserted an allow using a bare commit, which the new behaviour refuses
outcome: declaration corrected to four rather than left wrong; all four gained the trailer and go on asserting the same allow, none was weakened
significance: a true positive of the stage 2 mechanism against the person building stage 3, which is the only kind of evidence that a guard is not merely ceremony

summary: check-controls refused to run at all: I committed a new suite and left it out of controls.list
detail: writing test-check-flaky-trailers.sh before its implementation made the directory and the suite list disagree. check-controls.sh exited 1 with 'add it, or name the implementation for what it does' and ran NOTHING, rather than running twelve suites and reporting green
significance: INC-0011 was exactly this - a committed control suite never added to CI, so nine ran while ten existed. The fix caught its own author within a day of the same mistake recurring
design_point: refusing to run beats running a subset: a partial green is a wrong claim, an error is a correct one
